prior_orchestrator_verdict.rationale: All three lenses ran (blind, edge-case, acceptance against the ticket story and plan); the change implements AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 with no migration or contract edits, but the ticket's own regression test for AC2 (Session Detail skill_count equals the number of skill bars) is missing and plan Review Focus 5 claimed it was pinned, so one major patch finding remains. 15 lens items were dismissed after checking them against the code: exact-name matching (the ticket's duplicates are byte-identical names), window and scope worries (the kind-2 branch is session-scoped too, and the SQL ran on PG 14 and 17), class-list agreement (asserted by the live test), 'stale' comments that actually describe data sources, and test-brittleness remarks; none deferred. Accepted limitations, not blocking: the exclusion is existence-based per session and name, so a name with more kind-4 rows than kind-2 rows in one session loses the surplus from both lists (edge cases such as an old CLI without the dispatch event plus a model Skill call of the same name), and the correlated predicate's cost was not measured on production-sized data.

standards_review.notes: Both commits follow EPMCDME-####: Description (EPMCDME-17201: Classify slash-started skills as skills in Session Detail; EPMCDME-17201: Drop slash-started skills from slash commands in Tools and Models).

Ruff check and format are clean on the changed files; new helper is typed and sits beside _no_summary. The Module Cohesion guide prefers a new module over appending a new concern to a 900-line file: the new live test and its constants were appended to test_live_route_pricing.py although it is not about route pricing. The guide does not mark this blocking, so it is recorded, not raised as a finding.
The new SQL fragment is built from constant strings and fixed column names only; no request input reaches it, and it keeps the sel session scope.

findings.title: No test asserts skill_count equals skill bars
findings.problem: The ticket asks for a backend test where a session with a slash-started skill and a Skill-tool skill shows both as skills and a skill_count that matches (AC2). The only added test builds two skill bars from synthetic rows in _build_dispatches and never reads skill_count. The existing live dispatch test seeds three slash-started skills but does not compare detail skill_count with the number of skill dispatches either, and plan Review Focus 5 claims the agreement is pinned.
findings.impact: The original symptom (Skills = 1 while the timeline had no skill bar) is two independent code paths, the SQL skill_count and the handler's dispatch kinds. Without a test tying them together the mismatch can come back, for example if a dispatch row type is added, with every current test still green.
findings.recommendation: Assert detail["skill_count"] equals the number of dispatches of kind skill in the live session-detail test that already seeds inline, foreground-fork and grouped slash-started skills, and add one Skill-tool-started skill to that session if the existing helpers allow it. Put a new test in its own live test module if that is cleaner than extending test_live_route_pricing.py (standards note above).
